name: 2029-2035 Indiana Avenue — First Presbyterian Church (district draft; refined by T-3014)

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: Otis 1913 dates the building 1870-1873 and its last service 29 December 1912, so it stands across the 1904 target; the draft's phase keeps the study's 1904-1911 window (study ruling 11).

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body (u -43.700, v -27.890 m from the building's front and southernmost faces), set from the corner at local (1282.70, -3598.28): Indiana Avenue's measured east line (data/street_grid/1904.json) with its centre 10.06 m (66 ft) west of it; the church's front stands 2.97 m behind that line and its south face 0.14 m behind 21st Street's north line, the trace's own readings. Good to about the trace's 0.19 m pixel and the sheet's fit. Rotation 179.497 degrees squares the plan to the avenue.
placement.symbolic_location: 2029-2035 S. Indiana Avenue, the north-east corner of Indiana Avenue and East Twenty-first Street, on sheet 35's Indiana frontage.

footprint.note: The building's whole plan as the trace outlines it: the body with its buttresses, and the tower and porch block that steps south of it at the 21st Street corner; the main body (43.7 x 23.1 m) is draft_plan's first rectangle.

stories.note: Three draft storeys of 4.6 m over a 0.9 m floor stand the walls to 14.7 m, the sheet's printed 48 ft to the eaves; a church has no storeys, and the count only sets the wall height and the rows of openings.

construction.note: Brick: the sheet colours it pink.

parts.from: the church's body, buttresses included, under one gable to Indiana Avenue, as the Otis 1887 plate shows it (sheet 35 draws dashed hips; the T-3009 trace of sheet 35 (s35wfp-indiana_2029-b1), read in metres from Indiana Avenue's east line and East 21st Street's north line)

draft_plan.note: One rectangle, the body read off the trace in metres from Indiana's line and 21st Street's; the buttresses fold into it and the tower stands as a feature.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the site row: One gable over the body at 54 degrees, ridge east-west with its gable to Indiana Avenue, as the Otis 1887 plate shows it (sheet 35 draws dashed hips, which the photograph does not bear out): through T-3066's camera the gable's coping apex stands about 30.9 m over grade, and 54 degrees over the body's 23.1 m width puts the ridge at 30.6 m. The tower is the trace's square at the south-west corner, 6.0 m across its faces (the trace's 6.5 m block less its angle buttresses, which are T-3067's), its brick to 39.5 m where the photograph's gablets spring (a low 3.8 m pyramid stands for the gablets and corner pinnacles) and the slated octagonal spire out of them, 4.1 m across at its foot, to its cross at about 75.9 m (the photograph's finial top reads 76.5 m). The sheet's printed 90 ft (27.4 m) cannot be the spire's height over grade: the photograph puts the tip at five times the eave's height, the sheet's own 48 ft. The tower's sash stand where the photograph's openings are, a tall two-light window in the second stage (12.2-20.2 m) and the louvred belfry (27.7-36.8 m), on the west and 21st Street faces. The body's openings are the draft's sash in rows, not the church's lancets, which are T-3067's. The seed 72272670 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-district-background-3009.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The Otis history of 1913 dates the building and its use: Calvary Presbyterian Church laid its corner stone in November 1870, the united First Presbyterian Church finished it after October 1871, and the final service in it was held on 29 December 1912 (otis_1913_first_presbyterian_21st_indiana_1887, pp. 52-56 and 291-292); the 1911 sheet letters it '1st PRESBYN. CHURCH'. So it was the First Presbyterian Church on 1 July 1904.

citations.citation: "The First Presbyterian Church. Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street (1887)." Halftone plate facing p. 82 in Philo Adams Otis, The First Presbyterian Church, 1833-1913: A History of the Oldest Organization in Chicago (Chicago: Fleming H. Revell, 1913).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3009, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-3014 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the rules' site row (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3009). The church fills the 2029-2035 lot on Indiana Avenue at 21st Street: J. C. Cochrane's building for Calvary Church, begun in 1870 and finished by the united First Church about 1872-1873, used until December 1912 (Otis 1913). Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35 prints it 48 ft to its eaves with a slated spire marked 90 ft on its south-west tower. The Otis plate of 1887 (otis_1913_first_presbyterian_21st_indiana_1887) shows the west front and the tower whole, and its camera is solved in data/reference_views/first_presbyterian_church_2029_indiana/ (T-3066): the gable, the tower's stages and the spire stand to its heights. It is drafted as a site so that its walls, roof and tower are the church's heights and not a house's; T-3067 works the rest of the plate.
